dc51.title: Permissions tree: tri-state checkboxes
dc51.summary: A dev-console token page lists API scopes as a nested tree. Make it selectable with real tri-state checkboxes, then add a filter that keeps ancestors visible.
dc51.brief:
An acmecloud “New fine-grained token” page. PermissionsCard loads a nested scope tree from getScopes() (random 0.4–1.2 s) and renders it read-only with the recursive ScopeNode. Groups can be nested (Repositories → Contents → Read contents). There are 12 leaf scopes.

Read utils/tree.ts first: getLeafIds(node) and countLeaves(nodes) are already written and are the backbone of a good solution. components/Field.tsx wraps the form fields.

The trap in this one is what you store. If you store a checked flag for every node, you have to keep parents and children in sync by hand. If you store only the selected leaf ids, every group's state is a derivation.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next 4–5 and the change. Change (~27 min): a filter box.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–24 Core · 24–27 Next · 27–37 change · 37–40 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Selection is shared by the tree and the Generate button, so it lives in App as a Set of leaf ids only. A node's state is derived each render: count how many of getLeafIds(node) are in the set. All = checked, none = unchecked, some = indeterminate. Toggling any node gets its leaf ids: if they're all on, remove them, otherwise add them all. That one function handles leaves, groups and the indeterminate case. indeterminate isn't an attribute, so I need a tiny TriCheckbox with a ref and an effect that sets ref.current.indeterminate. For the filter I'll compute a Set of visible ids with a recursive walk and skip nodes not in it, so toggling still uses the full original nodes."
requirements: Every node (group and leaf) has a checkbox with its label as a clickable <label>. Clicking a leaf toggles it

Checking a group checks all of its descendants at every depth; unchecking a fully checked group clears them all. A group is checked when all its leaves are, unchecked when none are, and shows the native indeterminate dash (set via ref.current.indeterminate) when some are

The Permissions header shows “3 of 12 selected” (leaf scopes only, total from countLeaves). Generate token is disabled until there is a token name and at least one scope; clicking it shows “Token “ci-deploy” created with 3 scopes.”
Clicking an indeterminate group selects all of its descendants (it never clears them). Each group row also shows “2/5” of its own leaves
A Clear link next to the count (only when something is selected) empties the selection. Selected rows get the soft indigo background

change.title: Filter that keeps ancestors
change.html:
"Security reviewers search for one scope, like billing, and get lost in the tree."

  • Add a “Filter scopes” input under the card header. It matches label or id, case-insensitive.
  • A node is shown if it matches, if it's inside a matching group, or if it's an ancestor of a match (so “billing” shows Organization → Billing).
  • No match: “No scopes match “xyz”.”
  • While filtering, checking a group still selects all its leaves, including hidden ones, and its state still reflects all of them.

Hint: don't build a filtered copy of the tree; compute a Set of visible ids and skip the others while rendering.

hints: State: const [selected, setSelected] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set()); in App, leaf ids only. Pass selected and onToggle down through PermissionsCard into the recursive ScopeNode.
Per node, derive: const ids = getLeafIds(node); const on = ids.filter((id) => { return selected.has(id); }).length; then checked = on === ids.length, indeterminate = on > 0 && !checked.
Never mutate a Set in state. Copy it: setSelected((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); ...; return next; });

Search: mdn HTMLInputElement indeterminate. It's a property only, so: const ref = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null); useEffect(() => { if (ref.current) { ref.current.indeterminate = indeterminate; } });. Leaving out the deps array re-applies it after the browser clears it on click.
Toggle in one function: const allOn = ids.every((id) => { return prev.has(id); }); then delete all if allOn, else add all. Indeterminate falls into the “add all” branch for free.

Change: collectVisible(nodes, q, out) returns true if anything under nodes is visible. A match adds its whole subtree; a node whose children returned true adds itself (it's an ancestor). Then in the maps: if (visible && !visible.has(child.id)) { return null; }.
rubric: Stored only leaf ids; every group state is derived (no sync effects)
Reused getLeafIds / countLeaves instead of re-walking the tree by hand
Set the indeterminate DOM property through a ref, and knows why an attribute doesn't work
Immutable Set updates with the updater form
Indeterminate click selects all (and can explain the choice)
Filter computed during render; ancestors kept; toggles still act on the full subtree
Labels linked to inputs (htmlFor/id) so the whole row is clickable and accessible

dc52.title: Streaming AI chat with Stop
dc52.summary: A writing-assistant chat sends messages but never answers. Stream the reply token by token with a blinking cursor, a real Stop (AbortController) and polite auto-scroll.
dc52.brief:
Quill is an AI writing assistant. The thread, MessageBubble and Composer (Enter sends, Shift+Enter is a newline) already work, but handleSend only appends your message. There's a TODO where the reply should start.

Read api.ts carefully: streamReply(prompt, onToken, signal) calls onToken once per chunk (first token after 0.3–0.7 s, then every 15–60 ms) and resolves when done. If the signal is aborted it stops and rejects with an AbortError. Asking the same prompt twice returns a different answer. utils/id.ts has makeId.

This is the core interaction of every AI product. The interviewer will watch for: tokens appended with the updater form, the controller kept in a ref, AbortError treated as a normal outcome (not an error), and scroll that respects the reader.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next 4–5 and the change. Change (~28 min): Regenerate.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–22 Core · 22–28 Next · 28–37 change · 37–40 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"On send I append two messages at once: the user's, and an empty assistant message with status: 'streaming'. I keep its id in streamingId state, which drives the Stop button and disables sending. Each token does setMessages(prev => prev.map(...)) to append to that one message; it has to be the updater form because tokens arrive faster than renders. The AbortController goes in a ref: it's not something I render. Stop calls abort(); the promise rejects with AbortError and I mark the message 'stopped'. For scroll I track whether the user is at the bottom in an onScroll handler, and only scroll to bottom in an effect on messages when they are."
requirements: Sending adds your message and an assistant message that fills in token by token as streamReply emits, with a blinking amber block cursor at the end while streaming. Before the first token, show three pulsing “thinking” dots

While streaming, the Send button is replaced by a Stop button and Enter does not send (you can still type the next prompt). Stop aborts via AbortController: tokens stop immediately, the cursor disappears and a small “Stopped” pill appears under the partial answer
When the stream completes the cursor disappears and Send comes back. An AbortError is not shown as an error; any other rejection shows “Something went wrong”

Auto-scroll only if the user is at the bottom: new tokens keep the thread pinned to the bottom, but if the user scrolls up to read, the thread stays where they put it. Sending a new message always scrolls down
While streaming and scrolled up, a floating “↓ Jump to latest” pill appears; clicking it scrolls down and resumes following. Leaving the page mid-stream aborts the request (effect cleanup)

change.title: Regenerate the last answer
change.html:
"Users want a second opinion without retyping the prompt."

  • Under the last assistant message only, when nothing is streaming, show “↻ Regenerate”.
  • Clicking it clears that answer in place (same message, not a new one) and streams a new answer for the user prompt right above it, with the same cursor, Stop and scroll behaviour.
  • Stopping a regenerate leaves the partial new answer with “Stopped”.

Hint: if your streaming code is one function runStream(assistantId, prompt), this is ten lines.

hints: Message shape: type Message = ChatMessage & { status?: 'streaming' | 'done' | 'stopped' | 'error' }; Seed messages have no status.
Append both messages in one update: setMessages((prev) => { return [...prev, userMsg, assistantMsg]; }); then start the stream with the assistant id.
Search: mdn AbortController. const controller = new AbortController(); controllerRef.current = controller; streamReply(prompt, onToken, controller.signal). Stop is controllerRef.current.abort().
Each token: setMessages((prev) => { return prev.map((m) => { if (m.id !== id) { return m; } return { ...m, text: m.text + token }; }); }); Using messages from the closure would drop tokens.
.catch((err) => { if (err.name === 'AbortError') { finish(id, 'stopped'); return; } finish(id, 'error'); })

At bottom: el.scrollHeight - el.scrollTop - el.clientHeight < 40 in onScroll. Then useEffect(() => { if (atBottom) { el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight; } }, [messages, atBottom]); (search: mdn scrollHeight).
Cursor CSS: an inline-block 8×1em span with animation: blink 1s steps(1) infinite and @keyframes blink { 50% { opacity: 0; } }.
rubric: One streaming function reused by send and regenerate
Tokens appended with the updater form; no lost tokens
AbortController in a ref, aborted on Stop and on unmount
AbortError handled as a normal 'stopped' outcome, other errors surfaced
Sending disabled while streaming (button and Enter key)
Auto-scroll respects a user who scrolled up; threshold, not exact equality
Mentions accessibility: aria-busy while streaming, not announcing every token

dc53.title: Kanban: drag, drop, roll back
dc53.summary: A sprint board renders four columns. Add HTML5 drag and drop with an insert indicator, persist moves optimistically, roll back when the API refuses, then add a keyboard alternative.
dc53.brief:
Orbit, a sprint board. App loads the board with getBoard() (0.4–1 s) and renders Column → CardView. Nothing moves yet.

Read utils/board.ts before writing anything: findCard and the pure moveCardInBoard(board, cardId, toColumn, toIndex) already do the array surgery, and they're exactly what you need for both the optimistic move and the rollback. components/Toast.tsx is a ready-made presentational toast.

moveCard(cardId, toColumn, toIndex) takes 0.4–0.9 s. It rejects when you move an unassigned card (dashed avatar: ORB-44, ORB-45) into Done. Note how toIndex is defined: the position after the card is removed from its old spot.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next 4 and the change. Change (~30 min): keyboard moves.

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan out loud · 7–25 Core · 25–30 Next · 30–42 change · 42–45 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"All drag state lives in App next to the board: dragId and dropTarget = { columnId, index }. Each column is a drop zone: onDragOver must preventDefault(), and it computes the insert index by finding the first card whose vertical middle is below the pointer. I only set state when the target changes because dragover fires constantly. The column renders a 3px indicator at that index. On drop I convert the indicator index to the API's index (subtract one if moving down in the same column), then commitMove: remember where the card was, setBoard(prev => moveCardInBoard(prev, ...)), call the API, and on rejection move just that card back and show the toast. The toast clears itself with a timeout in an effect."
requirements: Cards are draggable. Dragging a card over any column shows a 3px indigo insert indicator where it will land (between cards, at the top, or at the end), the column tints, and the dragged card fades to 40%. Works across columns and within a column

Dropping moves the card immediately (optimistic) and calls moveCard with the correct index. Moving a card down within its own column lands exactly where the indicator was. Dropping where it already is does nothing and makes no API call

When the API rejects (unassigned card into Done), only that card goes back to its original column and position, and a toast shows the server's message (“Assign someone before moving ORB-44 to Done.”). The toast closes with ✕ or after 4 seconds
Indicator disappears when the drag leaves the column (not when it passes over a child card) and on drag end. dragover doesn't set state when the target hasn't changed

change.title: Keyboard alternative
change.html:
"Accessibility review: drag and drop is mouse-only. We need a keyboard path (WCAG 2.5.7)."

  • Cards are focusable. Enter or Space (or a click) picks a card up: it gets an indigo ring and the top bar shows “Moving ORB-41 · ← → change column · ↑ ↓ reorder · Enter or Esc to drop”.
  • While picked up, ←/→ move it to the previous/next column (same position, clamped), ↑/↓ reorder it within the column. Each move goes through the same optimistic save + rollback.
  • Focus stays on the card after it moves to another column. Enter or Esc puts it down.
  • Announce each move in a visually hidden aria-live region: “Moved ORB-41 to In review, position 1.”

hints: Search: mdn HTML drag and drop API. The three you need: onDragStart (call e.dataTransfer.setData('text/plain', id)), onDragOver (must call e.preventDefault() or drop never fires), onDrop.
Insert index: const els = e.currentTarget.querySelectorAll('[data-card-id]'); loop, and the first one where e.clientY < rect.top + rect.height / 2 is the index. None? It's els.length.

Render the indicator by building an array: cards.forEach((card, i) => { if (indicatorAt === i) { items.push(indicator); } items.push(<CardView ... />); }); then one more check for indicatorAt === cards.length.
Same-column move down: the indicator index counts the card you're dragging, the API index doesn't. if (from.columnId === to.columnId && from.index < index) { index -= 1; }
Rollback without clobbering other moves: setBoard((prev) => { return moveCardInBoard(prev, cardId, from.columnId, from.index); }); rather than restoring a whole saved board.
dragleave fires when moving onto a child. Guard with if (!e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget as Node)) { setDropTarget(null); }

Change: a card that moves to another column is a new DOM node, so focus is lost. useEffect(() => { boardRef.current.querySelector('[data-card-id="' + selectedId + '"]').focus(); }, [board, selectedId]); (with null checks).
rubric: Reused moveCardInBoard / findCard for the optimistic move and the rollback
preventDefault in dragover; state only updated when the drop target changes
Correct index math for moving down within a column (explained out loud)
Rollback is per-card (functional update), not a stale whole-board snapshot
Toast auto-dismiss in an effect with cleanup; restarts for a new message
Keyboard path: focusable cards, Enter/Space/Esc/arrows, focus restored after remount
aria-live announcement for moves and failures

notes: 12 · muted · right of the top bar

dc54.title: Production typeahead for docs search
dc54.summary: A docs site has a search box that does nothing. Build a real typeahead: debounce, cancel stale requests, cache, keyboard navigation, highlighted matches, and every state handled.
dc54.brief:
Tidewave docs. The header has a SearchBox (controlled input, nothing else). Sidebar and Article work; App owns the current page and passes onNavigate.

Read api.ts: searchDocs(query, signal, shouldFail) behaves like fetch: it takes an AbortSignal and rejects with an AbortError when aborted. Latency depends on the query: 1–3 characters take 0.6–1.1 s, longer ones 0.12–0.24 s, so responses can come back out of order. The “Simulate API failure” checkbox makes it reject. utils/text.ts has escapeRegExp, which you'll want for highlighting.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next 4–5 and the change. Change (~31 min): no spinner flicker.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–25 Core · 25–31 Next · 31–41 change · 41–45 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Everything stays inside SearchBox; the only way out is onNavigate. I'll write a tiny useDebouncedValue(query, 250) hook. One effect keyed on the debounced query does the fetch: empty → idle; in the cache (a Map in a ref) → use it; otherwise make an AbortController, set loading, call the API, and abort in the cleanup. That cleanup is what kills the race: a slow 'us' can never overwrite a fast 'use'. AbortError is ignored, other errors set an error state. Keyboard lives on the input: arrows move activeIndex, Enter navigates, Escape closes. The listbox gets combobox ARIA with aria-activedescendant, and options use onMouseDown preventDefault so the input's blur doesn't close the panel before the click lands."
requirements: Typing opens a results panel under the input. Requests are debounced 250 ms, and when a new query starts, the previous request is aborted through its AbortController. The results always belong to the latest query, even when an older, slower request would have finished last

Each result shows the title with the matching text wrapped in <mark> (case-insensitive), the section on the right, and a one-line snippet. Clicking a result opens that page in the article and clears the search

States: “Searching…” with a small spinner while loading; “No results for “xyz”” when empty; with the failure toggle on, “Search is temporarily unavailable.” plus a Retry button that tries again. An AbortError is never shown as an error

Keyboard: ↓/↑ move the highlighted result (wrapping), Enter opens it, Escape closes the panel (a second Escape clears the input). The first result is highlighted when results arrive. ARIA: role="combobox", aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant, and role="listbox"/"option" with aria-selected
Results are cached in memory by query: retyping a query you've searched shows its results without a network request. Pressing / anywhere outside a text field focuses the search box

change.title: No spinner flicker
change.html:
"Design says the spinner flashing on every keystroke looks broken. Most searches come back in 200 ms."

  • Show “Searching…” only if the request has taken longer than 300 ms. Fast queries (4+ characters) should never show it at all.
  • While a request is in flight but not yet “slow”, keep showing the previous results instead of blanking the panel.
  • Clean up the timer when the request finishes, is aborted, or the component unmounts.

hints: Debounce as a hook: useEffect(() => { const t = setTimeout(() => { setDebounced(value); }, delay); return () => { clearTimeout(t); }; }, [value, delay]);
Search: mdn AbortController and react useEffect race condition fetch. Create the controller inside the effect and return () => { controller.abort(); };
In .catch: if (err.name === 'AbortError') { return; } before setting the error state.

Cache: const cacheRef = useRef(new Map<string, DocHit[]>()); Check it at the top of the effect and cacheRef.current.set(q, hits) on success. A ref, because the cache itself never needs to re-render anything.
Highlight: text.split(new RegExp('(' + escapeRegExp(q) + ')', 'ig')). With a capture group, matches land at odd indexes: if (i % 2 === 1) { return <mark key={i}>{part}</mark>; }
Clicking an option blurs the input first. Put onMouseDown={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); }} on each option so focus stays and the click lands.
Change: a second piece of state, slow. In the effect: const t = setTimeout(() => { setSlow(true); }, 300);, clear it and setSlow(false) when the promise settles, and clearTimeout(t) in the cleanup.
rubric: Debounce extracted into a reusable hook
Abort in effect cleanup; explains the out-of-order race it prevents
AbortError ignored; real errors shown with a retry path
Cache in a ref keyed by normalized query
Complete combobox ARIA and keyboard model; mousedown/blur gotcha handled
Highlight uses escapeRegExp (a query like “(” doesn't crash)
Delayed loading indicator with timer cleanup; keeps stale results instead of flashing

dc55.title: Analytics grid: sticky, resizable, sortable
dc55.summary: A campaign report renders a plain wide table. Turn it into a real data grid: sticky header and first column, drag-to-resize columns with pointer events, and sorting. Then persist widths.
dc55.brief:
A marketing Campaign performance report. App loads 30 rows with getCampaigns() (0.4–1.1 s) and CampaignTable renders them inside a 480px-high scroll container. The table is wider than the container, so you can scroll both ways, and right now the header and campaign names scroll out of view.

Read columns.ts: every column has a key, label, default width, align and a render function that already formats the value (with utils/format.ts). Use it for everything; don't hard-code columns. StatusPill renders the status.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next 4 and the change. Change (~29 min): persist widths.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–24 Core · 24–29 Next · 29–37 change · 37–40 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Sticky is CSS: th { position: sticky; top: 0 } and the first cell of every row left: 0, with the top-left corner on the highest z-index. I know sticky table cells lose their borders with border-collapse: collapse, so I'll switch to separate with zero spacing, and give sticky cells a background. Widths live in state as { [key]: px }, applied through a <colgroup> with table-layout: fixed. The resize handle is a 7px span at the right edge of each header: pointerdown captures the pointer and stores startX and startWidth in a ref (it changes every move and never renders), pointermove sets the width with a minimum. Sorting is { key, dir } state and a sorted copy during render."
requirements: Inside the scroll container the header row stays visible when scrolling down and the Campaign column stays visible when scrolling right. The top-left header cell stays above both. Borders and backgrounds stay intact on sticky cells

Each header has a resize handle on its right edge (cursor: col-resize, 2px blue line on hover/drag). Dragging it changes that column's width live, using pointer events with setPointerCapture, never below 70px. Other columns keep their widths (the table gets wider/narrower)

Clicking a header sorts by that column: first click ascending ▲, again descending ▼, and so on. Numbers sort numerically (Spend by dollars, not by the formatted string). Inactive headers show a faint ↕, the active header turns blue, and <th aria-sort> is set
Resizing never triggers a sort, the page doesn't select text during a drag, and double-clicking a handle resets that column to its default width

change.title: Remember column widths
change.html:
"Analysts set up their widths every morning. Remember them."

  • Persist widths in localStorage under campaigns.columnWidths.v1 and restore them on load.
  • Save when a drag ends, not on every pointermove.
  • Storage can throw (private mode, quota) or contain garbage: wrap reads and writes in try/catch, ignore invalid values, and fall back to the defaults from columns.ts.

hints: Search: css position sticky table header border-collapse. You'll want border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 0; and a solid background on sticky cells, or rows show through.
Fixed widths: table-layout: fixed, a style={{ width: total }} on the table, and <colgroup>{COLUMNS.map((c) => { return <col key={c.key} style={{ width: widths[c.key] }} />; })}</colgroup>.

Search: mdn setPointerCapture. In pointerdown: e.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); dragRef.current = { key, startX: e.clientX, startWidth: widths[key] };. Then pointermove on the same handle keeps firing even off the handle.
Move: const w = Math.max(70, drag.startWidth + e.clientX - drag.startX); setWidths((prev) => { return { ...prev, [drag.key]: w }; });
Keep the handle a sibling of the sort button (not inside it), so a drag doesn't click the button. e.preventDefault() in pointerdown stops text selection.
Sort a copy: [...rows].sort((a, b) => { ... }), comparing a[key] - b[key] for numbers and localeCompare for strings.
Change: lazy initial state useState(loadWidths) so storage is read once. Save in an effect: useEffect(() => { if (resizingKey === null) { saveWidths(widths); } }, [widths, resizingKey]);
rubric: Knew (or found quickly) the border-collapse + sticky gotcha and z-index layering for the corner cell
Columns driven by the COLUMNS config, widths via colgroup + table-layout fixed
Pointer capture; drag bookkeeping in a ref, width in state; min width enforced
Resize handle doesn't trigger sort or select text
Sorted copy, numeric compare on raw values not formatted strings, aria-sort
localStorage wrapped in try/catch, validated, lazy-loaded, saved on drag end
Talked about performance (re-render per pointermove is fine at 30 rows; would throttle with rAF or virtualize at 10k)

notes: w 7 · line 1px #D5DBE5 · active 2px accent full height

dc56.title: Photo lightbox with focus management
dc56.summary: A photography portfolio shows a grid of thumbnails. Build an accessible fullscreen lightbox: arrow keys, Escape, a real focus trap, focus returned to the right thumbnail, and preloading. Then swipe.
dc56.brief:
Atlas, a photographer's field-notes site. App loads 12 photos with getPhotos() (0.4–1 s) and renders a grid of Thumbnail buttons. Clicking one does nothing yet.

utils/wrap.ts has wrapIndex(i, length), which makes ←/→ wrap around without off-by-one bugs. Each Photo has a src (full size) and thumb.

This one is mostly about focus. The interviewer will Tab around inside your dialog, press Escape, and check where focus lands. Plan that before you write the markup.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next 4–5 and the change. Change (~28 min): drag to swipe.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–22 Core · 22–28 Next · 28–37 change · 37–40 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"App owns openIndex: number | null. The lightbox is only rendered when it's not null, so mount and unmount are my open and close. Inside, a role="dialog" aria-modal container gets one onKeyDown: arrows call onChange(wrapIndex(...)), Escape calls onClose, and Tab is the trap: if focus is on the last button and you Tab, go to the first, and the reverse with Shift. On mount I focus the close button. To give focus back, I keep an array of thumbnail refs in App and focus thumbRefs.current[openIndex] in the close handler, which is the photo you were viewing, not necessarily the one you clicked. Preloading is an effect on index that creates new Image() for the neighbours."
requirements: Clicking a thumbnail opens a fullscreen dark lightbox (role="dialog", aria-modal="true") with the full image, a caption (title in italic serif, location in small caps) and a counter “4 of 12”
←/→ keys and the round ← → buttons show the previous/next photo, wrapping from 12 to 1 and 1 to 12. Escape and the ✕ button close it
On open, focus moves into the dialog (the ✕ button). Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the dialog: from the last control Tab goes to the first, and the reverse
On close, focus returns to the thumbnail of the photo that was showing (open #4, press → twice, close: focus is on thumbnail #6)
The next and previous images are preloaded (new Image().src = ...) whenever the index changes, so arrowing is instant

change.title: Drag to swipe
change.html:
"Half our traffic is on tablets. People try to swipe."

  • Pressing on the image area and dragging horizontally moves the image with the pointer (pointer events, so mouse, pen and touch all work).
  • Releasing after more than 60px left goes to the next photo, more than 60px right goes to the previous one; less than that snaps back with a short transition.
  • No transition while dragging (it should track the pointer exactly), and the browser's native image drag must not kick in.

hints: State: const [openIndex, setOpenIndex] = useState<number | null>(null); Render <Lightbox index={openIndex} onChange={setOpenIndex} onClose={handleClose} /> only when it's not null.

Ref array for thumbnails: const thumbRefs = useRef<(HTMLButtonElement | null)[]>([]); and pass a callback ref: buttonRef={(el) => { thumbRefs.current[i] = el; }}. The Thumbnail puts it on its button: ref={buttonRef}.

Search: focus trap react keydown tab or WAI-ARIA dialog modal pattern. In the dialog's onKeyDown: get dialogRef.current.querySelectorAll('button'), and if !e.shiftKey && e.target === last, e.preventDefault(); first.focus();
Initial focus: useEffect(() => { closeRef.current.focus(); }, []); in the Lightbox. Give the dialog tabIndex={-1} so clicks on empty space keep focus inside.
Preload: useEffect(() => { [wrapIndex(index + 1, n), wrapIndex(index - 1, n)].forEach((i) => { const img = new Image(); img.src = photos[i].src; }); }, [index]);

Change: search mdn pointer events setPointerCapture. Start x in a ref, dragX in state for the translateX. On pointerup compare dx to ±60. Add draggable={false} on the img and touch-action: pan-y on the stage.
rubric: Lightbox mount/unmount = open/close; index lives in App
Uses wrapIndex; no off-by-one at the ends
Correct dialog ARIA and initial focus
Focus trap handles Tab and Shift+Tab at both ends
Focus returns to the currently viewed photo's thumbnail (ref array)
Preloads neighbours in an effect
Swipe uses pointer capture, threshold, no transition while dragging, native drag disabled

notes: title italic serif 24 · location 12 uppercase accent

dc57.title: Shared checklist: optimistic edits + conflicts
dc57.summary: A shared festival checklist is read-only. Make toggle, rename and delete instant with optimistic updates, roll back per task when the server refuses a stale version, and offer Reload. Then a batch action with partial failure.
dc57.brief:
The HarborFest vendor checklist is shared by four organizers. App loads tasks with getTasks(); TaskRow renders a checkbox (read-only), the title, “Last edited by”, and a ✕ that does nothing.

Read api.ts closely. Every Task has a version. updateTask(id, patch, version) and deleteTask(id, version) (0.4–0.9 s) succeed only if you send the version the server has; otherwise they throw a ConflictError. Simulation: right after you load, Priya edits task #3 (“Confirm food truck lineup”) in another tab, so any write to #3 conflicts until you fetch it again with getTask(id).

A successful updateTask returns the saved task with its new version. If you don't keep it, your next edit to the same task conflicts with yourself.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next 4 and the change. Change (~31 min): Mark all done.

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan out loud · 7–25 Core · 25–31 Next · 31–42 change · 42–45 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Tasks stay in App. Client-only flags (saving, conflicts) go in separate maps keyed by id, not on the Task, so server copies can replace tasks wholesale. I'll write one saveTask(task, patch): apply the patch locally, mark saving, call updateTask with the version I have; on success replace with the server's task (new version); on failure replace with the original task I was handed, and if it's a ConflictError flag the row. While a row is saving I disable it so I can't fire a second write with a stale version. Delete removes it and re-inserts at the old index on failure. Reload calls getTask and clears the flag. If saveTask resolves true/false instead of rejecting, the batch is just Promise.all."
requirements: Toggling the checkbox updates the row and the “2 of 6 done” progress instantly, then saves with updateTask. While saving, the row is faded, says “Saving…”, and its controls are disabled. On success the row shows the server's copy (new version, “Last edited by You”)

When a save fails, only that task rolls back. A ConflictError also shows an inline amber message under the title: “Someone else changed this · Reload”. Reload fetches the latest with getTask (Priya's new title appears) and clears the message; after that, edits to #3 save normally
Delete (✕) removes the row immediately and calls deleteTask. If it fails, the task reappears in its original position (with the conflict message for a conflict)
Clicking a title turns it into an input (autofocused). Enter or blur saves the rename optimistically through the same path; Escape cancels; an empty or unchanged title doesn't save

change.title: Mark all done (partial failure)
change.html:
"The night before the event, organizers want one button."

  • Add a Mark all done button next to the progress bar (disabled when everything is done).
  • It marks every open task done at once (optimistic), saving each one with its own request.
  • Tasks that fail roll back individually and get the conflict message; the others stay done.
  • When all requests settle, show a summary line under the header: “Marked 3 of 4 tasks done. 1 couldn't be saved.”

hints: Client-only flags: const [saving, setSaving] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({}); and the same for conflicts. Read with Boolean(saving[t.id]).
Replace one task: setTasks((prev) => { return prev.map((t) => { if (t.id !== next.id) { return t; } return next; }); });

One write path: saveTask(task, patch) returns updateTask(...).then(() => true).catch(() => false) (with braces + return, plus the rollback in the catch). Then every caller, including the batch, reuses it.
Conflict check: if (err instanceof ConflictError) { ... }. Import the class itself (not import type), because instanceof needs the runtime value.
Delete rollback: remember index before removing, then next.splice(Math.min(index, next.length), 0, task) on a copy.
Inline edit state belongs in TaskRow (editing, draft): nothing else needs it.
Change: search mdn Promise.allSettled. If saveTask never rejects, Promise.all(targets.map((t) => { return saveTask(t, { done: true }); })) gives you an array of booleans to count.
rubric: One optimistic write function reused by toggle, rename and batch
Rollback is per task (restore that task), not a stale snapshot of the whole list
Keeps the server's returned version; disables a row while saving to avoid self-conflicts
ConflictError handled distinctly with a recovery path (Reload)
Delete restores at the original index
Client-only flags kept out of the server model
Batch reports partial failure accurately

dc58.title: Filter popover with pending selections
dc58.summary: An architecture studio's project list has a dead Filter button. Build a popover with status and owner checkboxes, search, Select all/Clear, Apply/Cancel draft semantics, removable chips and a count badge. Then sync to the URL.
dc58.brief:
Studio Varga's project list. App loads 18 projects with getProjects() (0.4–1 s) and renders ProjectList. The toolbar has a Filter button that does nothing.

Read utils/list.ts: toggleInList is exactly what a checkbox needs, and uniqueSorted builds the owner options from the data. STATUSES in api.ts is the fixed status list. StatusBadge and Initials already render rows.

The key product rule: selections in the popover are a draft. Nothing changes in the list until Apply; Cancel, Escape or clicking outside throws the draft away.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next 4–5 and the change. Change (~28 min): URL sync.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–22 Core · 22–28 Next · 28–36 change · 36–40 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Two copies of the filters. applied lives in App because the list, chips and badge all read it. The draft lives inside a FilterPopover component that's only mounted while open, initialised from applied. So opening gives a fresh copy, Apply calls onApply(draft), and Cancel just unmounts. No syncing effects. The popover listens on document for Escape and mousedown outside (ignoring the Filter button itself, or it would close and reopen). Closing returns focus to the Filter button through a ref. Chips and the badge are derived from applied. Empty selection in a group means 'any'."
requirements: Filter toggles a popover anchored under it with a Status section (6 checkboxes) and an Owner section (one checkbox per owner, from the data, sorted) with a Search people input that filters the owner list (“No one matches …”)

Checking boxes changes only the popover. Apply filters the list (status OR within a group, AND across groups; an empty group means any) and closes. Cancel, Escape and clicking outside close without applying, and reopening shows the applied selection again

Active filters appear as chips above the list (“Status: Design ✕”, “Owner: Hana Sato ✕”); ✕ removes one immediately, Clear all removes all. The Filter button shows a dark count badge (“3”) when filters are active, and the toolbar says “5 of 18 projects”
Each section has Select all and Clear. For owners they act on the visible (searched) owners only. No matches at all: “No projects match these filters.” with a Clear all button
Focus moves into the popover when it opens and returns to the Filter button when it closes. The button has aria-expanded and aria-haspopup

change.title: Shareable filter URLs
change.html:
"PMs paste links to filtered lists in Slack, and the filters are lost."

  • Whenever the applied filters change, write them to the query string as repeated params: ?status=Design&status=On+hold&owner=Hana+Sato, using history.replaceState (no new history entries).
  • Keep any other query params and the #hash intact.
  • On load, initialise the applied filters from the URL.

In this practice IDE the preview shares the page URL, which is exactly why you must not clobber other params or the hash.

hints: Draft without sync effects: render <FilterPopover applied={applied} ... /> only when open, and inside do const [draft, setDraft] = useState(applied);. Every open is a fresh copy.
Checkbox: setDraft((prev) => { return { ...prev, statuses: toggleInList(prev.statuses, value) }; });
Outside click: document.addEventListener('mousedown', ...) and if (popRef.current.contains(e.target)) { return; }. Also ignore the Filter button (pass its ref), or its own click reopens the popover.
If onCancel is a dependency of the listener effect, wrap it in useCallback so the listeners aren't re-added every render.
Filtering: (applied.statuses.length === 0 || applied.statuses.includes(p.status)) && (same for owners), computed during render.
Change: search mdn URLSearchParams getAll and mdn history.replaceState. Read with new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).getAll('status') in a lazy useState(fn).

Writing: const url = new URL(window.location.href); url.searchParams.delete('status'); applied.statuses.forEach((s) => { url.searchParams.append('status', s); }); history.replaceState(null, '', url.toString()); keeps everything else, hash included.
rubric: Draft vs applied separated; popover mount = fresh draft; Cancel needs no code
Reused toggleInList / uniqueSorted; options derived from data
Escape + outside click with listener cleanup; anchor excluded
Focus into popover and back to the trigger; aria-expanded
Chips, badge and count derived from applied state
Select all/Clear scoped to visible owners
URL sync with replaceState, repeated params, other params and hash preserved, lazy init

dc59.title: Booking date range picker
dc59.summary: A cabin booking page shows one static month. Build a two-month range picker: click check-in then checkout, hover preview, past and booked nights blocked, a range that can't cross a booked night, and a live summary. Then arrow-key navigation.
dc59.brief:
Fernhill Cabins, booking “The Alder Cabin”. App loads availability with getAvailability('alder') (0.4–1 s): a price per night and a list of unavailable nights as ISO strings. MonthView renders one month of day buttons, display only.

Read utils/date.ts first, it does the date math so you don't have to: TODAY (a fixed Mar 3 2026; never use new Date() for today), toISO/fromISO, addDays, addMonths, getMonthGrid, formatShort and nightsBetween. Note the comment: ISO date strings compare correctly with < and >, so keep selections as strings. utils/money.ts has formatPrice.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next 4 and the change. Change (~31 min): keyboard navigation.

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan out loud · 7–25 Core · 25–31 Next · 31–42 change · 42–45 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"State in App: viewMonth (first of the left month), start and end as ISO strings or null, and hover. Everything else is derived per day: disabled if it's before TODAY, booked, or, while I'm picking a checkout, on or after the first booked night after start; that's the rule that stops a range crossing a booking. Click logic: no start or a finished range → new start; a day on or before start → move start; otherwise it's the end. The range to draw is end, or the hovered day while picking. I'll pass a getInfo(iso) function down so MonthView stays dumb, and render it twice."
requirements: Two months side by side (March and April 2026 to start) with ‹ › buttons that move both by one month. ‹ is disabled on the current month. Today (Mar 3) is bold and underlined

Click a day to set check-in, then a later day to set checkout. Start and end are dark green circles, the nights in between light green. Clicking a day on or before check-in moves check-in; clicking after a complete range starts a new one. While choosing checkout, hovering previews the range

Past days (before the fixed TODAY) and booked nights (struck through) can't be selected. Once check-in is set, every day on or after the next booked night is disabled too, so a range never includes a booked night
Summary bar: “Add your check-in date” → “Mar 4 → Add checkout” → “Mar 4 → Mar 9 · 5 nights” with “$925 total” (1 night is singular). Clear dates resets; Reserve is enabled only with a full range

change.title: Keyboard navigation
change.html:
"Accessibility audit: the calendar is a wall of 60 tab stops, and you can't use it without a mouse."

  • Only one day is in the Tab order (roving tabIndex): today at first, then the last day you focused or clicked.
  • ←/→ move one day, ↑/↓ one week, across month boundaries; going past the visible months shifts the view. Focus never goes before today.
  • Enter/Space select like a click, and arrowing while picking a checkout shows the same range preview as hovering.
  • Disabled days must still be focusable (you arrow over them): switch from disabled to aria-disabled and ignore clicks on them yourself.

hints: Keep dates as ISO strings in state: useState<string | null>(null). Comparisons are just iso < TODAY_ISO, iso > start.
The crossing rule: const later = availability.unavailable.filter((u) => { return u > start; }).sort(); then while picking an end, disable any iso >= later[0].
Click logic in order: if (!start || end) { setStart(iso); setEnd(null); } else if (iso <= start) { setStart(iso); } else { setEnd(iso); }
Preview: let rangeEnd = end; if (start && !end && hover && hover > start && !isDisabled(hover)) { rangeEnd = hover; } and a day is in range when iso > start && iso < rangeEnd.
Two months: render <MonthView month={viewMonth} /> and <MonthView month={addMonths(viewMonth, 1)} />. Pass a getInfo(iso) function rather than five props per day.
Change: search roving tabindex and WAI-ARIA date picker dialog example. Store focusedIso; give that button tabIndex={0} and all others -1.

After an arrow key the button may be in a month that wasn't rendered yet, so focus it in an effect: calendarRef.current.querySelector('[data-date="' + focusedIso + '"]').focus(), guarded by a ref flag so it only runs after keyboard moves.
rubric: Reused the date helpers; never called new Date() for today
ISO strings in state; comparisons are simple and correct
Disabled rules derived (past, booked, beyond next booking)
Click state machine handles restart and earlier-day cases
Hover preview computed, not stored as a range
Summary pluralises and totals with formatPrice
Roving tabindex, aria-disabled instead of disabled, focus follows arrows across months

dc60.title: Capstone: AI chat conversation sidebar
dc60.summary: The sidebar of an AI chat app lists conversations flat. Group them by date, add search, inline rename, delete with a 5-second Undo (deferred API delete) and New chat. Then pinning.
dc60.brief:
The capstone. Lumen is an AI chat app. App loads 14 conversations with getConversations() (0.4–1 s), sorts them newest first and renders a flat list of ConversationRows. Selecting works and ChatPane shows the selected chat. The New chat button and the search box do nothing.

Read utils/date.ts: NOW is fixed (Mon Jun 15 2026, 2 pm) and daysBetween(earlier, later) counts calendar days, which is what grouping needs. In api.ts, note that deleteConversation is permanent; the server has no undo, so Undo has to happen before you call it.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next 4–5 and the change. Change (~32 min): pinning.

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan out loud · 7–26 Core · 26–32 Next · 32–41 change · 41–45 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The list is a pipeline computed every render: filter by search → sort by updatedAt → bucket with a groupFor(c) function → render the groups in a fixed order, skipping empty ones. Nothing derived goes in state. Delete with undo: remove it from state immediately, start a 5-second timer that calls the API, and keep { conv, timer } in a ref so Undo can clearTimeout and put the conversation back. A small pending state drives the toast. If a second delete happens during the window I finalise the first one right away, and on unmount I flush it. If the deleted chat was selected I select its neighbour in display order. Rename is local edit state in the row with an optimistic update. New chat calls the API, prepends and selects."
requirements: Conversations are grouped under Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days (2–7 calendar days before NOW) and Older, newest first inside each group. Empty groups are not shown
Search chats filters by title (case-insensitive) and the groups recompute; nothing matching shows “No chats match “xyz””

Hovering or focusing a row reveals actions. Delete removes the chat immediately and shows a toast “Chat deleted · Undo” with a draining 5 s bar. Undo restores it in its place. The API delete is called only after 5 s without Undo. Deleting the selected chat selects its neighbour
Rename (✎ or double-click) swaps the title for an input with the text selected. Enter or blur saves (optimistic, then renameConversation), Escape cancels, an empty title is ignored

+ New chat calls createConversation (shows “Creating…” and is disabled meanwhile), adds “New chat” at the top of Today, selects it and clears the search. Deleting a second chat while a toast is open deletes the first one for real immediately; leaving the page flushes a pending delete

change.title: Pinned conversations
change.html:
"Power users keep a few long-running chats. They want them at the top."

  • Add a pin action to each row. Pinned chats appear in a Pinned section above Today, whatever their date, newest first.
  • Unpinning returns a chat to its date group. Pinning does not change updatedAt.
  • Optimistic via setPinned(id, pinned), rolled back on failure. The pin icon is purple while pinned. Search and delete/undo keep working with pinned chats.

Hint: if grouping is one function, this is one more if at the top of it and one more entry in the group order.

hints: Grouping: function groupFor(c) { const days = daysBetween(new Date(c.updatedAt), NOW); if (days <= 0) { return 'Today'; } if (days === 1) { return 'Yesterday'; } if (days <= 7) { return 'Previous 7 days'; } return 'Older'; }
Bucket into an object, then render a fixed order: GROUP_ORDER.map((g) => { const items = groups[g]; if (!items) { return null; } return <section key={g}>...</section>; })

Search: mdn setTimeout clearTimeout. The undo timer must be cancellable from a different handler, and changing it must not re-render: const pendingRef = useRef<{ conv: Conversation; timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> } | null>(null);

Delete: commitPending(); setConversations(remove); const timer = setTimeout(() => { commitPending(); }, 5000); pendingRef.current = { conv, timer }; setPending(conv);. commitPending reads the ref, clears it, hides the toast and calls the API.
Undo: clearTimeout(p.timer), clear the ref and toast, then setConversations((prev) => { return [...prev, p.conv]; }). The sort puts it back in its old position for free.
Rename input: autoFocus plus onFocus={(e) => { e.target.select(); }} selects the text. Keep editing/draft in the row.
Draining bar: a 3px element with animation: drain 5s linear forwards and @keyframes drain { to { transform: scaleX(0); } }. Give the toast key={pending.id} so the animation restarts for each delete.
rubric: Search → sort → group pipeline derived during render; groups in fixed order, empty ones skipped
Used NOW and calendar-day math, not Date.now() or 24h arithmetic
Deferred delete: timer in a ref, API only after the window, Undo cancels
Edge cases: second delete during the window, unmount flush, deleting the selected chat
Inline rename with Enter/Escape/blur and optimistic update
New chat: loading state, prepends, selects, clears search
Pinning as one extra rule in groupFor, optimistic with rollback
